note: The Watchtower review desk's adjudication record. Every checker flag gets a verdict here before the queue is cleared: what was fetched, what it showed, and why the guide's record did or did not change. A flag is a signal, not a fact — nothing in models.json moves without a verdict in this file (or a documented promotion in model-updates.md). Hand-authored; preserved across build_api.py rebuilds.

failed_source_reviews.basis: Re-probed 2026-10-12: Medium (3 models), MarkTechPost (3), GlobeNewswire (2), Morningstar (1) all still 403 the checker's user agent; x.ai and midjourney.com 403 as JS-app homepages. Every one is third-party coverage or a marketing homepage — in all 13 partial records at least one official source answered, so no record went dark (the run's with_errors, which counts only all-sources-failed, was 0). The failures stay on the records, honestly, as 'partial'.

pakera.pk (timeout in the run) answered 200 on re-probe; the monid-ai GitHub page (503 in the run) answered 200; Luma's three timeouts (TechTimes, mivicai, lumalabs.ai itself) all answered 200. One-off network weather, not dead sources.
failed_source_reviews.group: Transient failures that recovered on re-probe

failed_source_reviews.basis: abnewswire.com dropped the connection (Hailuo) and returned 503 (Wan 2.6) — the wire is flaky for automated clients this week; europesays.com dropped the connection again; whatsnew.fyi rate-limited (429) the shared ComfyUI release page. All third-party; each model's official sources answered. Left in place and on the record; if abnewswire fails a third consecutive run it should be swapped for another wire copy of the same releases.

flag_reviews.basis: The moved source is a third-party startup directory listing (added Oct 6), re-fetched intact — its signature still matches the flagged run, so the 'move' was the listing's own page churn against the older baseline. It asserts the model exists; it is not a ByteDance source. No official announcement, model card, or pricing exists. The record's standing position (reported, unconfirmed — watch ByteDance Seed's own directory) is unchanged.

The flagged source is the klingai.com homepage. Re-fetched: its hero now leads with 'All-New Kling 4.0' — the move is the 4.0 banner, not anything about 3.0. This is the exact churn Watchtower 2.1 already adjudicated: the homepage is signature-excluded from this run on (still fetched and recorded). Nothing in the 3.0 record moved.
Same klingai.com homepage move as Kling 3.0 (one rotating hero flags every Kling model that watches it). The homepage is signature-excluded from this run on. Nothing in the 2.5 Turbo record moved.

The moved source is an ABNewswire press-release review of the Hailuo Video Agent — third-party wire copy, not a MiniMax page. On re-fetch the wire no longer answers the checker at all (connection dropped; the same wire 503s on Wan 2.6's item). No official MiniMax source moved, and no price or version fact in the record is contradicted. Record unchanged.

The moved source is a competitor's comparison post (Magic Hour's blog). Its Luma figures ($10/mo, $35 tiers) match the plans already on record; nothing in it postdates or contradicts the record. No Luma source moved. Record unchanged.

The moved source is Magic Hour's Pika pricing roundup. Re-fetched: 'Pika Create starts at $10/month for Starter; commercial licensing starts at Creator, $35/month' — Pika's published plans, and the figures already on record. A third-party roundup agreeing with the record is not a change. Record unchanged.

The moved source is a CometAPI aggregator post about the (June 2025) V1 launch. It moved twice within an hour — the delta is rotating site chrome (a 'now live on CometAPI' banner), not the article. Verified-noisy: the URL joins the signature-exclusion list in model-check-config.json from this pass (fetched and recorded every run; the watch reads the Krea and Outlook pieces plus the news feed). No Midjourney source moved. Record unchanged.

The strongest-looking flag, and it does not clear the bar the standing watch set in advance. The klingai.com hero leads with 'All-New Kling 4.0 — Try Now', but that banner was already up on Oct 11 when three reviewers (wavespeed's Oct 1 evidence review, orcarouter, this guide) verified it exposes no price, date, or resolution text and only Flash early access is live. The CryptoBriefing piece is coverage of the Sept 28 unveil and the Kuaishou spinoff listing, not a GA event; the pakera.pk piece states plainly 'Kling 4.0 is not fully out yet.' Still no GA model ID in the official API docs and no published pricing (APIMart lists pricing as unannounced). Record stays 'announced' — Flash early access for Ultra Yearly subscribers, full model expected this October. The standing watch item stays open.

reviews.method: Each flagged URL was re-fetched with the checker's own fetch path (scripts/refresh/check_models.py fetch/clean_text) on 2026-10-12 and read against the model's record. Failed sources were re-probed the same way. Promotion criteria were the ones written in advance: a status flips only on an official source showing the change (for Kling 4.0, the standing watch item requires a GA model ID in the official API docs or published pricing).
reviews.outcome: No promotions. Zero records in models.json or pricing.json changed: all 8 flags were third-party churn, an already-excluded homepage, or — Kling 4.0 — a launch banner that does not meet the pre-written GA criteria. One source (CometAPI's Midjourney post) joined the signature-exclusion list. The checker re-run after this pass establishes the new baseline (see model-checks.json); the queue returns to its 5 standing hand-authored watches.
reviews.reviewer: Watchtower 2.2 review pass (agent, following the promotion workflow in scripts/refresh/check_models.py)
reviews.scope: All 8 changed-source flags from the 2026-10-12T23:00Z checker run (the first full-coverage run, Watchtower 2.1), plus the 13 partial records carrying a failed source in the same run.

flag_reviews.basis: All 17 flags trace to signature-unstable surfaces, proven two ways. (1) GitHub blob pages: fetching one flagged page twice in a row returned two different signatures (99786a5e vs 086a1f46) — the pages embed per-request nonces, so no run can ever match the last; github.com is now excluded from the signature globally (config defaults), the same treatment klingai.com got per-model in 2.1. (2) The remaining movers are blog posts, press-release rails, and live listing pages (higgsfield.ai blog + help-center, openrouter.ai model pages, magichour.ai's release tracker, einpresswire/sloptvnews/usanewshour/webdisclosure/digitaltoday news pages, orcarouter's release-date blog, runcomfy's model page) whose related-content rails and live stats rotate between fetches; each is now excluded per-model in model-check-config.json with a dated note; four more surfaces that moved again in the calibrated re-run (Magic Hour's blog for Pika, an Outlook news page for Midjourney, the bfl.ai homepage for FLUX 3, a syndicated story page for vivago R1, and a dev.to review for FLUX 3) were excluded in a second pass the same night. No official pricing page, API doc, or model card moved for any of the 17, and no record was contradicted. All 17 stay fully watched — every source is still fetched and recorded each run; the exclusions only stop chrome from crying wolf. Models: Soul 2.0, Soul Cinema, Soul Cast, Seedance 2.5, Kling 3.0, Veo 3.1, Wan 3.0 / 3.0 Prime, MiniMax H3, DoP, Marketing Studio video, Grok Imagine Video 1.5, Kling 4.0, LTX-2.5, Vidu S2, Mirage Tesseract, Vidu Q4 Preview, FLUX 3 Video.

reviews.method: The post-review re-baseline run flagged 17 models — nearly the same set on a second, single clean run, which ruled out a one-off network flake and pointed at the surfaces themselves. Two consecutive fetches of a flagged GitHub blob page (the checker's own fetch path) returned different content signatures, proving per-request instability. Each non-GitHub mover was identified from the run's moved_urls and classified by page type before exclusion.
reviews.outcome: No promotions, no record changes. github.com excluded from the change signature globally; 26 blog/listing/homepage URLs excluded per-model across three calibration passes (the second added an exact-URL anchor (a trailing $ in the exclusion entry) so bfl.ai's homepage could be excluded without touching its pricing page, which stayed put and stayed watched). The checker was re-run with the calibrations in place to establish the published baseline: 1 changed, 0 errors, 0 unwatched. The one flag is Vidu S2, raised on a third-party blog (lapaasvoice.com) in the final run — left standing in the queue for the next review pass, and shown on the board as a review item. The 10 remaining board alerts are the adjudicated partial records: third-party sources that bot-block the checker while each model’s official sources answer.
reviews.scope: The 17 changed-source flags raised by the re-baseline checker runs of 2026-10-12 (~23:34Z), immediately after review pass 1 cleared the 2.1 queue.
